metadata.title: Round 2 SME Review Packet
metadata.subtitle: Combined Round 2 focus group · the benefits competency shared by design and administration
metadata.time_required: About 35 minutes for this focus group

how_this_works.what_we_did: We combined your Round 1 edits, comment by comment, into one proposed version of each competency. The shared compliance anchor was reauthored and the service-operations competency was kept and sharpened; both are applied (Part A). The one item that needs the design and administration groups together, the shared Benefits Program Strategy competency, is drafted as a recommendation (Part B).
how_this_works.what_we_need: Confirm the two applied changes in Part A. In Part B, settle the shared-spine middle ground for Benefits Program Strategy: who owns design and governance, who administers, and which operational components move out. Nothing in Part B is final until you decide.
how_this_works.where_feedback_went: Every Round 1 comment on these competencies is in the appendix disposition, including the Benefits design-owner edits and the Benefits Administration request for a middle ground that reads for both design and administration.
how_this_works.status_intro: Every competency below carries a status label so you can see, at a glance, what is already settled and what still needs the group. Items are grouped into two parts: Part A holds changes we have already applied (read and confirm); Part B holds the items for live discussion (decisions and proposals).

ground_rules.text: Decide who designs, governs, or administers, and at what level, before debating wording. Wording fixes already handled in the edit lane do not need this room.

Benefits owns the design and governance of benefits and well-being programs; Leave & Benefits Administration administers them. Place each role on the ladder, and let the essential functions in the job descriptions separate the levels, rather than splitting the shared competency in two.
Owners and dates recorded at sign-off feed the decision registry; the sub-family owner is John.

coverage.legend: D designs and owns (Levels 3 to 4) · C carries with the specialization lens · F facilitates · U uses and applies (Levels 1 to 2) · A advises (apply-and-advise) · Aw awareness (Levels 1 to 2) · S shared employment-practice anchor · L2 limited (Level 2).
coverage.note: This matrix shows the complete union of competencies touched by both specializations. Benefits Program Strategy & Management is shared: Benefits owns design and governance (Levels 3 to 4); Leave & Benefits Administration administers (Levels 1 to 2); the essential functions in each job description separate the levels. Compensation & Pay Design is carried by Benefits at advise level (owned by Compensation in Total Rewards); Payroll Operations & Compliance is carried by Leave & Benefits Administration at use levels (owned by Payroll); Workforce Analytics & HR Insights is used by both at a reporting level, not built. These carried competencies were settled in Round 1 and are included here for completeness — read them in the appendix; only Benefits Program Strategy needs a decision this session. The Payroll and HR Operations statutory-operations spine (tax, pension, social-security, and labour law applied to payroll, benefits, and leave) is held in the HR competency library and is not built by this pairing.

ratings_legend.heading: How to read the Round 1 ratings
rows: Essential
Jobs in this specialization cannot perform core work without this capability. Absence equals role failure.
Very important
Jobs perform noticeably better with strong capability. Weak capability creates measurable friction and rework.
Important
Useful and expected, but not a differentiator. Other competencies carry more weight day to day.
Limited
Occasionally relevant. Not a reliable predictor of performance for this specialization.
Low
Rarely relevant. Borderline for inclusion in this specialization.

note.text: The competency is shared across the Benefits and Benefits Administration specializations. The aim is one set of indicators that reads for both, with the job-description essential functions separating the levels, not two competencies.

rows: Change this to Benefits Program Strategy, Design and Governance and move more operational components to HR Service Delivery Excellence or HR Compliance & Workforce Risk. (361 insertions, 170 deletions synthesized.)

This competency will be shared across Benefits and Benefits Admin specializations, so we'll need to find a middle ground that reflects the Benefits competency required within both, and let the essential functions in the job descriptions separate out the levels.

items.recommendation: Keep this as the shared benefits competency across design and administration. Benefits owns design and governance at Levels 3 to 4; Leave & Benefits Administration administers at Levels 1 to 2; the essential functions in each job description separate the levels, so the indicator wording holds a middle ground that reads for both. Resolve the rename to Benefits Program Strategy, Design and Governance, and move the operational components the design owner flagged to HR Service Delivery Excellence and HR Compliance & Workforce Risk. The v5 wording already merges the well-being, governance, and mobility additions (see appendix).

decide.text: Adopt the rename? Confirm the design-at-Levels-3-to-4 and administer-at-Levels-1-to-2 split, with job-description essential functions separating the levels? Which operational components move out, and to which competency?

rows: Operational components of Benefits Program Strategy
Benefits design owner: move operational components to HR Service Delivery Excellence or HR Compliance.
HR Service Delivery Excellence receives the operational components; the shared competency keeps design and governance.
Statutory operations (Payroll spine)
Payroll, HR Operations, and Leave & Benefits Administration share statutory-operations competencies (tax, pension, social-security, and labour law applied to payroll, benefits, and leave).
Held in the HR competency library under the Payroll and HR Operations spine; not built by this pairing.

competencies.name: Benefits Program Strategy & Management
competencies.note: Shared by Benefits (design and governance) and Leave & Benefits Administration (administration); v5 wording merges well-being, governance, and the mobility dimension; rename and operational scope are open (Decision 1).

indicators.text: Demonstrates foundational understanding of benefits and well-being programs, including eligibility rules, plan provisions, leave rules, and mobility requirements.
Prepares and maintains benefits records, leave files, assignment packets, vendor intake materials, and program documentation within established processes and governance standards.
Records employee elections, mobility case updates, vendor responses, and documentation evidence in benefits systems.
Supports implementation and communication of program changes.
Administers benefits, leave, wellness, and mobility cases using plan rules, mobility policies, and service procedures.
Supports program updates, vendor activities, and policy changes through coordination with internal stakeholders and external partners.
Reviews market data, utilization trends, employee feedback, and vendor performance to identify design and operational optimization opportunities.
Applies plan provisions, governance standards, compliance requirements, and applicable labor agreements when supporting the design and strategy of benefits and well-being programs.

Designs benefits, well-being, and mobility program improvements using market insights, utilization data, vendor performance metrics, employee feedback, and business objectives, while balancing compliance, financial risk, and labor and union considerations.
Leads complex leave, benefits, and international assignment reviews involving policy, tax, payroll, immigration, and vendor inputs.
Evaluates vendor performance, plan effectiveness, cost trends, workforce needs, and employee impact to support strategic recommendations and benefits design decisions.
Leads cross-functional initiatives involving benefits design, vendor strategy, governance improvements, and employee experience enhancements.

Establishes enterprise strategies, governance frameworks, cross-functional operating standards, and stakeholder alignment models for benefits, well-being, and mobility programs in alignment with workforce and business priorities.

Defines and drives benefits strategy, vendor governance, financial risk management, employee engagement, and program optimization to improve employee experience, business outcomes, and long-term cost sustainability.
Integrates analytics, market insights, compliance considerations, and workforce trends to guide enterprise benefits decision-making.

Sponsors large-scale benefits transformation initiatives, including program innovation, communication strategies, and continuous improvement to strengthen governance, operational effectiveness, employee experience, and business outcomes.
